steps.title: Someone to talk to
steps.body: Conversations belong to characters. A character placed on a map is a neighbour the hero can walk up to and talk to (T). You add Old Tom, a villager, next to where the hero arrives; then you write what he says.
steps.task: Add Old Tom to the map.

how.text: In Characters a new character starts from a preset (+ New character). Here Brix's helper makes Old Tom from the Chef preset and places him near the arrival spot.

do.say: Old Tom joins the game, next to the arrival.

steps.title: A new conversation
steps.body: The Dialogue tab shows the game's conversations. + New (under Conversations, on the left) writes one for the open character and puts it in his Talk list, so talking to him plays it.
steps.task: Open the Dialogue tab, then press + New under Conversations.

how.text: Click the Dialogue tab at the top of the middle area.

do.say: The Dialogue view of the Character studio.

how.text: Under Conversations on the left, press + New. A conversation called “Old Tom talk” opens with one line.

do.say: + New writes a conversation for Old Tom.

steps.title: Write it as a script
steps.body: Script shows the conversation as plain text for writers: == starts a section, “Old Tom (happy): …” is a line, * lines are the options of a choice (-> where each goes), > lines are actions (add, give, like), and [if …] makes anything conditional. Apply puts it back.
steps.task: Open Script, write Old Tom's conversation, press Apply.

args.script:
== start
[if talks > 0] Old Tom (happy): Back again, {hero.name}?
Old Tom: Welcome, traveller! Mind the bridge, it wobbles.
* What bridge? -> bridge
* Buy a map (5 gems) [if gems >= 5] [grey] -> map
* Bye! -> end

== bridge
> like +5
Old Tom: The old one to the east. Cross it slowly.

== map
> add gems -5
> give map
Old Tom (happy): Here you go. Don't get lost!

how.text: Click Script in the bar above the conversation.
Replace the text with Old Tom's script: a greeting that changes the second time (talks > 0), a choice of three, and two sections the options lead to. Press Apply (or Ctrl Enter).

do.say: Type the script here, then Apply.

steps.title: The same, as a list
steps.body: List shows each step as a row: who says it and their mood, the text, and an “if” chip; choices show their options with where each goes. Graph shows sections as boxes with arrows. All three views edit the same conversation.
steps.task: Click List, then Graph, to see the same conversation two other ways.

how.text: Click List: the script became rows you can edit one by one.

do.say: Each line, choice and action is a row.

how.text: Click Graph: start, bridge and map are boxes, the options are arrows.

do.say: Sections as boxes, choices as arrows.

steps.title: Try every branch
steps.body: Preview plays the conversation here. Under “Try it with…” set the values its conditions read: talks (how often the hero talked to Old Tom before) and gems. With 0 gems “Buy a map” is greyed out; with 5 it works.
steps.task: Press ▶ Preview and play the conversation.

how.text: Press ▶ Preview at the top right of the conversation. Click the box to move on, click an option to pick it.

do.say: The conversation plays beside the editor.

steps.title: How it looks
steps.body: Project › Dialogue sets the look for the whole game: eight styles, text speed, the voice blip and its pitch, lines that move on by themselves, portraits and colours. A conversation can still pick its own style.
steps.task: In Project › Dialogue, pick Speech bubbles.

how.text: Open the Project tab (right) and scroll to Dialogue.

steps.title: Talk to Old Tom
steps.body: In Play, walk up to Old Tom and press T (or E). Enter, Space or a click moves on; 1–3 or the arrows and Enter pick an option. Esc, or walking away, ends it. Logic can react with On choice made and On conversation end.
steps.task: Press Play, walk to Old Tom and press T.

how.text: Walk to Old Tom (he stands near the arrival) and press T.

do.say: The hero walks over and talks.

steps.title: Your characters talk
steps.body: Old Tom has a conversation with a choice, a condition and actions, in the game's dialogue style. Signs can hold a conversation too (select a sign, “Read with E”), objects can start one from an interaction (Start conversation), and logic can start one (Start conversation, category Dialogue).
